beats.label: S1 · The recruit
beats.text: Joe recruits Cruz Manuelos, a Force Recon Marine, into the CIA's Lioness program to infiltrate Aaliyah, daughter of terrorist financier Amrohi.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the operator, the target, and the whole premise of the season and series.

beats.label: S1 · Inside the circle
beats.text: Cruz endures brutal SERE training, then successfully befriends Aaliyah in Chesapeake and is folded into her private social world.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes that Cruz is inside Aaliyah's life — the position everything later depends on.

beats.label: S1 · Kyle's Texas mess
beats.text: Kyle borrows Joe's QRF for an off-books cartel extraction that goes public, drawing scrutiny from Westfield and DHS onto the Lioness team.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Kyle as Joe's dangerous freelancer and puts Westfield's control over the QRF on the table.

beats.label: S1 · Cleaning it up
beats.text: The team kills an Al-Qaeda cell in San Antonio to bury the fallout; Neal notices a scratch on Joe's face and starts guessing what she really does.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The domestic crack in Joe's marriage opens here and stays open for the rest of the series.

beats.label: S1 · The Hamptons weekend
beats.text: Cruz spends a weekend alone with Aaliyah that ends in a kiss. Joe forces her to compartmentalise and stay on mission toward the Mallorca wedding.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The mission becomes emotionally impossible for Cruz here; everything at the wedding is powered by this compromise.

beats.label: S1 · Made at the wedding
beats.text: At Aaliyah's wedding in Mallorca, Ehsan uses facial recognition on an old track photo to expose Cruz as a Marine just as she meets Amrohi alone.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The blown cover and the accidental encounter with the target are the hinge the whole finale turns on.

beats.label: S1 · Cruz walks away
beats.text: Cruz kills Ehsan and Amrohi with a kitchen knife, fights Joe during extraction, and severs ties, condemning the program for making the next generation of terrorists.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Defines Cruz's state going into next season and Joe's reason to reconsider her whole role.

cliffhanger.text: The Amrohi mission succeeded and destroyed Cruz. She has cut Joe off, Joe is questioning the Lioness program, and Neal is quietly certain his wife kills people for a living.
questions: Will Cruz ever work with Joe again after what Mallorca cost her?
Can Joe keep running Lioness now that she doubts what it does?
How long can Joe's marriage to Neal survive what he now suspects?

characters.name: Joe McNamara
characters.line: CIA Lioness station chief; ran Cruz's op to a bloody success and is now reconsidering her role in the program.

characters.name: Cruz Manuelos
characters.line: Marine-turned-Lioness who killed Amrohi and his son-in-law with a knife, severed ties with Joe, and denounced the mission.

characters.name: Aaliyah Amrohi
characters.line: Amrohi's daughter and Cruz's target, in one night widowed of Ehsan and orphaned of her father by the woman she loved.

characters.name: Kaitlyn Meade
characters.line: Senior CIA supervisor over Lioness, married to financier Errol, who weighed and approved the kill on Amrohi.

characters.name: Byron Westfield
characters.line: CIA Deputy Director of Operations who owns Joe's QRF and pushed the White House to authorise Amrohi's assassination.

characters.name: Kyle McManus
characters.line: CIA operator whose off-books Texas extraction created the fallout Joe's team then had to clean up in San Antonio.

characters.name: Neal McNamara
characters.line: Joe's husband and paediatric oncologist, increasingly disturbed by what he now believes she does on deployment.

beats.label: S2 · Hernandez taken
beats.text: Los Tigres cartel abducts Congresswoman Hernandez in Texas; the CIA extracts her and identifies China's MSS as the hand steering the cartel.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the season's target (Los Tigres) and the geopolitical frame (China via Mexico) in one move.

beats.label: S2 · The niece
beats.text: Joe recruits Army pilot Josephina Carrillo, niece of cartel head Alvaro, to infiltrate her estranged father Pablo, a lawyer laundering for the family.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the new Lioness and the family lever the whole plan depends on.

beats.label: S2 · Cruz shadows Carrillo
beats.text: Cruz returns as a Delta Force SFC to shadow Carrillo, whose loyalty Joe distrusts after she's caught lying about speaking Spanish and her family ties.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Brings Cruz back onto the team and establishes the guarded partnership at the season's centre.

beats.label: S2 · The trafficked children
beats.text: A warehouse raid uncovers cartel sex trafficking; Joe defies orders to intercept the children at the border and the operation ends in a suicide bombing.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Joe openly defying Westfield and Meade, and the personal cost that sets up her injury.

beats.label: S2 · Joe's goodbye call
beats.text: Carrillo turns Pablo, but Joe is quietly shot in the op and, believing she is dying, calls Neal from the plane to say goodbye before Walter Reed saves her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The near-death and the phone call are what force Joe and Neal back toward each other by the finale.

beats.label: S2 · Pablo takes the cartel
beats.text: Meade flips Pablo entirely: he executes his brother Alvaro at the Monterrey compound and inherits Los Tigres as a US-controlled asset, delivering the MSS agent.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Installs a CIA-owned cartel boss in Mexico — the biggest board change of the season, still live going forward.

beats.label: S2 · The Iran strike
beats.text: Cruz and Carrillo bomb an Iranian convoy of Chinese nuclear scientists; their helicopter is downed and the team is nearly overrun before the 82nd Airborne rescues them.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the season on an act of war against Iran and China that no next season could ignore.

cliffhanger.text: Pablo now runs Los Tigres for the CIA, Chinese scientists and an MSS agent are dead in Iran, and Joe — nearly killed on the border — has come home to Neal, who told her she'll always have a home to return to.
questions: How long will Pablo Carrillo stay a loyal US-controlled cartel boss?
Will Iran or China retaliate for the convoy strike, and against whom?
Can Joe keep doing this work after nearly dying and hearing what Neal said?

characters.name: Joe McNamara
characters.line: Still running Lioness; shot during the Pablo operation and welcomed home by Neal after being told she always has one.

characters.name: Cruz Manuelos
characters.line: Now a Delta Force SFC pulled back onto the team to shadow Carrillo, and by season's end sleeping with her.

characters.name: Josephina Carrillo
characters.line: Former Army pilot turned Lioness who broke her family open so the CIA could install her father atop the cartel.

characters.name: Pablo Carrillo
characters.line: Cartel money-launderer flipped by the CIA; killed his brother Alvaro and now runs Los Tigres as a US asset.

characters.name: Kaitlyn Meade
characters.line: Senior CIA supervisor who engineered Pablo's turn, absorbed the MSS agent, and kept the White House on-side.

characters.name: Byron Westfield
characters.line: CIA Deputy Director of Operations who authorised the Iran convoy strike against Chinese nuclear scientists.

characters.name: Kyle McManus
characters.line: CIA operator running interrogations for the team; cleared Gutierrez and remains Joe's closest field partner.

characters.name: Neal McNamara
characters.line: Joe's husband, shaken by her goodbye call from the plane, told her she'll always have a home to come back to.
